intended_object: The inertia group (stabilizer) of a representation A of a normal subgroup N ⊴ G, from Clifford theory: I_G(A) = {g ∈ G | the conjugate representation ᵍA (x ↦ A(g⁻¹xg)) is isomorphic to A}. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition takes the stabilizer of `toSkeleton A`, the isomorphism class of A, under the action of G on `Skeleton (FDRep k N)`. That action is induced by the conjugation functor `conjNormalFDRepFunctor g = Action.res (MulAut.conjNormal g⁻¹)`. The conjugate ᵍA is therefore the representation x ↦ A.ρ(g⁻¹xg), which is the standard conjugate. `mem_inertia_iff` proves directly from the definition that g ∈ inertia A ↔ Nonempty (ᵍA ≅ A), so this is exactly {g | ᵍA ≅ A}. It is a subgroup because it is a stabilizer, and the library proves that it contains N. No irreducibility hypothesis is imposed, which matches the general definition in the literature; irreducibility is only needed for later results.

On generality: k is only assumed to be a ring, and the representations are finite-dimensional (`FDRep`). This is the standard setting of Clifford theory. The construction could also be written for arbitrary `Rep k N`, but it is mainly used for finite-dimensional or irreducible representations, so restricting to `FDRep` is not a real loss of generality. Mathlib has no inertia-group or Clifford-theory definition for representations of normal subgroups.
